crbcc compiles R code to byte code. It gives the same byte code as the
compiler package of R, but it is faster. This vignette shows how to use
crbcc for a closure, for the installation of packages and for the JIT of R.
For the performance of crbcc, refer to the
[benchmark report](https://prl-prg.github.io/crbcc/benchmarks.html).

## Compile a closure

`cmpfun()` compiles a closure, as `compiler::cmpfun()` does.

```{r}
library(crbcc)

f <- function(x) {
  s <- 0
  for (i in seq_len(x)) s <- s + i
  s
}

cf <- cmpfun(f)
cf(10)
```

The result is the same as the result of the compiler package:

```{r}
identical(cf, compiler::cmpfun(f), ignore.bytecode = FALSE)
```

`compile()`, `cmpfile()` and `loadcmp()` work as the functions of the
compiler package with the same names. For the compiler options, refer to
`?cmpfun`.

## Install packages with crbcc

R CMD INSTALL compiles the closures of a package to byte code. To make it
use crbcc, enable the R CMD INSTALL hook before the installation:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
enable_r_cmd_install_hook()
install.packages("MASS")
enable_r_cmd_install_hook(FALSE)
```

`enable_r_cmd_install_hook()` sets the environment variable `R_PROFILE_USER`
to the hook. The R processes that this R session starts read this file.
While the hook is enabled, these R processes do not read your `.Rprofile`
file.

To install a package from a shell, set `R_PROFILE_USER` for R CMD INSTALL:

```sh
R_PROFILE_USER=$(Rscript -e 'cat(crbcc::r_cmd_install_hook_path())') R CMD INSTALL foo_1.0.tar.gz
```

If crbcc cannot compile a closure, the hook compiles it with the compiler
package.

**Note:** crbcc compiles only the packages that R installs from source. A
binary package is already compiled. On Windows and with the R for macOS
from CRAN, `install.packages()` installs binary packages by default. To
install from source, use `install.packages(..., type = "source")`.

## Use crbcc in the JIT

The JIT of R compiles a closure or a loop before R runs it. A function
`enable_jit()`, which makes the JIT use crbcc, is ready but not active.
It changes two functions of the compiler package. The CRAN policy permits
this change only with the agreement of the maintainer of the compiler
package, and we do not have this agreement yet.
